laws.rule: You must carry ID such as a passport or residence permit, particularly when driving or in a taxi. Police forces regularly ask for ID.
laws.heading: Personal ID

laws.rule: There are severe penalties for all drug offences. Local prison conditions are harsh.
laws.heading: Illegal drugs and prison sentences

laws.rule: Same-sex sexual relationships are not criminalised. However, Guinea-Bissau is a conservative society and same-sex couples showing affection in public may attract unwanted and negative attention. Read more advice for LGBT+ travellers .
laws.heading: LGBT+ travellers

laws.rule: Guinea-Bissau is a cash-based economy. Credit cards are rarely used and there are not many ATMs in the country. If you need to exchange foreign currency, use an official bureau de change.
laws.heading: Money

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: FCDO's laws and cultural differences section for Guinea-Bissau has no customs or etiquette guidance. A national etiquette page has not been searched for yet. Ask locally. The IBAP code of conduct for the Bijagos says not to photograph sacred sites (balobas, sacred groves) unless your guide allows it, and to ask before photographing people. Give gifts through the lodge, not directly. Some sacred islands are open only to initiated elders.
